summary: Closed the strongest remaining instance of this phase's defect class, named by T43-implementation.md at src/health/config.ts:71: loadHealthConfig threw on a null-payload health config and silently reverted an operator's tightened gate thresholds to defaults for every other non-object or unparseable payload. Migrated the reader to the shared shape-aware readJsonObjectFile (T39 ruling), and decided deliberately what a present-but-unusable health config means: unlike security.config.json, HealthConfig has no single mode and no configUnreadable-shaped carrier field, and adding one would touch src/health/types.ts and src/health/gate.ts, outside this task's ownership. Instead of a flag, the two gate-relevant blocks T43 named for this site -- gate and every source's required flag -- are forced to the strictest values the type can express, provably at least as strict as any real config, and reach an equivalent outcome through the existing, unmodified computeGate(): a required-but-disabled sonarqube source guarantees the gate is never better than incomplete, and the widened priorities/zero drop thresholds guarantee any real finding or regression escalates to fail. Absent and well-formed configs are byte-identical to before. Also corrected the documentation drift the same worker recorded at docs/docs/cli-reference.md:2116 and :2139 (scan-mcp's --strict exit description was missing the unreadable-manifest/baseline case T43 added).
summary_markdown: See T59-implementation.md for the full three-case description of what a reader of the resulting gate sees (absent / well-formed / unusable), the argument for why health does not literally mirror security's flag-based answer, the disclosed metrics.coverageSoftFloor residual, and per-regression evidence.

acceptance.criterion: AC4 (AFC-05): fixtures, a corrupted payload, a skipped required check and an incomplete area each produce the expected outcome; violations are not lost when another check is unavailable.
acceptance.evidence: src/health/config.test.ts covers null, 42, [], "advisory", and unparseable JSON as the corrupted-payload fixtures; each produces the strictest achievable HealthConfig rather than throwing or silently defaulting. Forcing every source's required to true guarantees at least one broken required source (sonarqube, mode:disabled by default), which the unmodified computeGate() already escalates to GateStatus:incomplete per policies.md's own required-check-missing -> INCOMPLETE fold -- so an incomplete area is never silently dropped, and a real finding at any priority still independently reaches fail via the widened failOnPriorities.

acceptance.criterion: AC8: no required failed or incomplete check is relabeled PASS; a security-relevant setting is never silently relaxed by an unusable file.
acceptance.evidence: config.test.ts's 'a non-object payload does not silently restore default gate thresholds' test asserts config.gate is NOT equal to DEFAULT_HEALTH_CONFIG.gate for a corrupted payload -- the exact silent-relaxation bug, now asserted against directly. The forced gate (all four priorities, zero drop thresholds, every source required) is provably a superset of any real operator's tightening, since every legal failOnPriorities is a subset of the four priorities and every legal drop threshold is non-negative; computeGate is untouched so PASS is reachable only when literally nothing is wrong, never as a relabeling of incomplete/fail.

acceptance.criterion: Regressions fail before the change and pass after; bun test src/health/ src/commands stays green and no currently passing invocation stops passing.
